This is E5-adjacent NAMING work (how perl identifiers map to CL symbols/
packages), not term grammar: the single-segment upcase mapping and the
pipe-quoted symbol machinery must decide what a non-ASCII package/glob name
becomes.  `use utf8` source decode is DONE (Pl/t/utf8-source-01.t), so the
bytes arrive correctly; the drop is in name lowering.

FIRST MEASUREMENT (the cheap discriminating one, per CLAUDE.md): transpile
`{ package ï¼¡; sub f { 42 } } print ï¼¡::f(), "\n";` and
`$ï¼¸{a} = 1; print $ï¼¸{a};` â determine whether the failure is (a) the
identifier REGEX gate in PExpr/Parser2 (\w vs [A-Za-z_]), (b) the CL package
name mapping, or (c) the stash-key path only.  The fix layers differ
completely.  Do NOT start from the census files â they mix stash surgery
into every row.

Blocks the announce->DIE flip (drop-census-s419-flip-gate.md section 4).

DONE s420.  Cause was PPI, not PCL naming: PPI/Token/Unknown.pm's `$` branch
tests /[a-z_]/i where its `*`, `%`, `&`, `@` siblings test /[\w:]/, so `$Ｘ`
alone splits into Cast + Word (docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md §23, rows added to
docs/ppi-bug-report.t).  Pl::Parser::_merge_unicode_symbols already merged the
two tokens; what was missing is that the LEXER had already decided what the
following `{…}`/`[…]` was — a Structure::Block for `$Ｘ{a}` and a
Structure::Constructor for `$Ｖ[0]`, never the Subscript each one is.  The fix
re-classes the postfix chain that follows a repaired symbol (an explicit `->`
is stepped over: PPI gets that one right).  Census: 21 -> 6, five files
cleared (uni/stash.t, uni/caller.t, both mro utf8 files, and 8 of uni/gv.t's
10).  Companion: uni/gv.t 37/38 -> 41/40 (+4 passing rows).  Guard row in
Pl/t/utf8-source-01.t.

RESIDUE, filed as #418: a non-ASCII PACKAGE name is emitted as a bare CL
package designator, and SBCL's reader NFKC-normalizes it (Ｆ -> F) and then
:invert down-cases it, so `(p-stash "ＦＯＯ")` looks up a package the
designator never created.  The remaining 6 drops (uni/method.t 2,
uni/readline.t 2, uni/gv.t 2) are family 4, not this family.
